title: Branching Canary Timeline — visual sandbox for multi-variant rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an interactive ‘branching timeline’ prototype for Redwood Console that lets operators compose multi-variant rollouts (canary -> branch -> ramp -> merge/rollback) as a single visual flow. The sandbox should make branching decisions explicit (split, pause, merge), surface safety gates and checkpoints, and allow simulated traffic playback to preview user-facing impact before applying changes. Focus is on a compact timeline canvas that scales to dozens of routes and integrates with the rollout rules panel and metric overlays.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Clickable timeline canvas that supports creating a new canary, splitting it into multiple variants, and merging back.
2) Visual encoding for traffic %, live/paused state, and safety-gate failures.
3) Hover and expand to see variant details (model version, kernel profile, % traffic, metrics snapshot).
4) Playback mode that simulates traffic over time and shows metric overlays (latency, error rate, cost).
5) Exportable JSON describing rollout graph for the backend rollout engine; links to an example GitHub PR.
6) Prototype validated with PM & Eng in review session and updated based on feedback.
7) Accessibility: keyboard navigation across timeline nodes and color-blind friendly palette.
comments: 2025-03-10 — Aisha Patel: Initial spike completed. Built low-fidelity wireframes for branching nodes + playback controls. Chose a horizontal timeline over a graph view to reduce cognitive load for operators who think in time ranges.

2025-03-11 — Marco Chen: Reviewed wireframes with Eng (S. Nguyen, R. Alvarez). Main trade-off is visual complexity vs. expressiveness — Eng prefers the timeline to output a normalized DAG for the runtime instead of a free-form graph to simplify rollback semantics.

2025-03-12 — Aisha Patel: Updated prototype to produce a canonical DAG export (nodes + edges + traffic buckets). Added nodes for safety gates with pass/fail badges. Uploaded interactive prototype to Figma and linked PR for a serializer spec.

2025-03-13 — PM review (Lina Morales): Suggested in-prototype experiments: fast rollback button, canary templates (e.g., quick 1% -> 5% ramp), and a ‘what-if’ mode to preview cost delta. Added to backlog as follow-ups.

2025-03-14 — Design critique: Accessibility pass required — adjusted color palette for color-blindness and added keyboard focus states. Engineering noted a potential performance issue when rendering 200+ nodes; agreed to lazy-render lanes and clip invisible nodes.
2025-03-14 — Marco Chen: Placed prototype into In Review; requested Eng feedback on export format (see PR #92) and asked for integration points with rollout API (runtime-1.18).
review_feedback: Eng (S. Nguyen): Approve concept; require deterministic DAG export and a strict validation step before rollout apply.
PM (Lina Morales): Love playback; please add a snapshot compare view for metrics at merge points.
Security (E. Rao): No immediate concerns, but audit log hook should capture timeline changes and who triggered playback/apply.
Design Lead (Maya Thompson): Refine node affordances — use compact badges for quick state at-a-glance, expand for details; reduce vertical spacing to keep visible context.
Support (D. Patel): Add inline help copy for new users and a link to release notes for rollback behavior.
Accessibility (R. Kaur): Keyboard-only flows OK after fix; check ARIA labels on play/pause and node controls.
next_steps: Incorporate Eng feedback into Figma prototype (deterministic DAG export + validation UI).
Add metric snapshot compare panel and cost projection overlay for the playback mode.
Partner with Runtime team to finalize export schema and add integration tests (action: create ENG sub-issue).
Run 2 user sessions with internal platform PMs and SREs next week, capture blockers and update acceptance criteria.
Prepare design handoff package and component spec for timeline nodes, badges, and keyboard interactions.
